tiles.name: calibration
tiles.result: SHORT, OPEN and LOAD at the jacks' pins and a 19.8 mm THRU: a full SOLT calibration; the 25 ohm standard then reads |S11| = 1/3 (9.5 dB return loss)
notes: Calibration standards at the board surface.  SHORT: the centre pin poured to ground all round.  OPEN: the bare pin
(fringing about 30 fF, to be measured against the NanoVNA's SMA open).  LOAD: 4 mm of 50 ohm line into 2 x 100 ohm.
25 OHM: 2 x 49.9 ohm at the end of 4.75 mm of line, a verification standard (VSWR 2).  THRU: 19.8 mm of 50 ohm line,
about 115 ps (enter it as the thru's delay).  Every jack on the boards is the same part, so a calibration here
measures each tile from its pads with its jacks taken out.

tiles.name: two loads
tiles.result: 200 OHM: Gamma = +0.6 (VSWR 4) at every frequency below 100 MHz.  MATCHED: Gamma = 0 at 9.2 MHz, |Gamma| 0.5 at about 5 and 14 MHz
notes: An L-network: 1.5 uH in series from the jack, 150 pF and 200 ohm to ground.  Z = j w L + 200 / (1 + j w 200 C) is 50 ohm
where w 200 C = sqrt(3), 9.2 MHz; away from it the point circles the chart.  The 200 ohm alone is the unmatched load.

tiles.name: resistive splitter
tiles.result: -6.0 dB from IN to each OUT, DC to 6 GHz, every port 50 ohm; OUT 1 to OUT 2 also -6 dB (no isolation)
notes: Three 16.9 ohm (50 / 3) from a star to the three ports: each port sees 16.9 + (16.9 + 50) / 2 = 50 ohm, and each
output gets half the input's voltage.  Symmetric, so any port is IN.  Compare P17's transformer splitter (3 dB, 25 dB
of isolation, 0.5-400 MHz).

tiles.name: transformer splitter
tiles.result: -3.1 to -3.4 dB from SUM to each port, 0.5-400 MHz; 25-34 dB between port 1 and port 2 (the datasheet)
notes: Mini-Circuits ADP-2-1+: a transformer splitter (a centre-tapped winding with a resistor across its ends), so the two
ports are isolated from each other: a combiner for two generators (the two DACs into one amplifier, for a two-tone
intermodulation test) as well as a splitter.  Pins 2 and 5 are joined and must not be grounded.

tiles.name: quarter-wave stub
tiles.result: a notch near 2.45 GHz (and 7.35 GHz) 20 dB or more deep; 0 dB at DC, -3 dB about 0.6 GHz either side
notes: An open stub a quarter wavelength long looks like a short circuit at its other end: the line from IN to OUT is
shorted at its middle at 2.45 GHz.  At DC and at 4.9 GHz (a half wave) it is open and the line passes.  The length
is 17.3 mm for an effective permittivity of 3.1; the coplanar line's real one moves the notch a few percent.

tiles.name: low-pass
tiles.result: 0.3 dB at 500 MHz, 0.8 dB at 1 GHz, 3 dB at 1.3 GHz, 26 dB at 1.5 GHz, 30 dB from 1.9 to 5 GHz (the datasheet)
notes: Mini-Circuits LFCN-1000+, an LTCC low-pass in a 1206: a MAX2871 at 915 MHz has its second harmonic 30 dB down
after it, and the synthesizer's square-ish output becomes a sine.

tiles.name: detector
tiles.result: about 1 mV out for -30 dBm in and 0.1 V for -10 dBm (square law, then linear toward 1 V at +10 dBm), 10 MHz to 6 GHz
notes: A voltage doubler of two zero-bias Schottky diodes (SMS7630: Is 5 uA, so about 5 k of video resistance each with
no bias).  Below about -20 dBm the output voltage is proportional to the RF power; above it, to the amplitude.
Read OUT with the ADC at high impedance: 50 ohm would short it.  Compare the AD8318's log output on RF-MOD-2.

tiles.name: bias-T
tiles.result: RF to RF+DC within 1 dB from about 2 MHz to 3 GHz; the DC loop's voltage on RF+DC, none on RF
notes: 100 nF passes the RF and blocks the DC; 10 uH + 330 nH + 27 nH pass the DC and block the RF (each inductor for its
own decade: 10 uH is 630 ohm at 10 MHz, 27 nH 400 ohm at 2.4 GHz).  Up to 100 mA (the 330 nH's rating) and 16 V (the
capacitors').  A bench supply's clips on the DC and GND loops.  Never put RF+DC into a jack that cannot take the DC.

tiles.name: step attenuator
tiles.result: 0 to 31.75 dB in 0.25 dB steps (1.5-2.8 dB of loss at 0 dB, rising with frequency), set by an 8-bit word over the Pmod; 31.75 dB at power-up
notes: pSemi PE43711 in serial mode: shift 8 bits (bit 7 = 0, then 4 x dB, least significant first) on SDATA (IO2) with
SCLK (IO3) while LE (IO4) is low, then raise LE.  RF-MOD's MAX2871 and TRF3722 take the same three lines' timing.
Below 48 MHz it takes less power: about +9.5 dBm under 0.5 MHz and +15 dBm at 5 MHz (+23 dBm above 48 MHz).

tiles.name: oscillator
tiles.result: about 10.5 MHz with TUNE at 0 V, 9.6 MHz at -2 V and 11.5 MHz at +2 V; about -22 dBm into 50 ohm; locks to a tone on TUNE within a few kHz of it
notes: A Clapp oscillator: the emitter follower's 220 pF / 220 pF divider feeds back what the series LC (10 uH and the
BB133) passes at its resonance, f = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L C)) with C the three capacitors in series.  The varactor's
cathode is at (3.3 V + TUNE) / 2, so TUNE tunes it (an FM transmitter from a DAC, or the control of a PLL closed in
the FPGA); a tone on TUNE near f also couples through 2.2 pF and the oscillator locks to it over a range that grows
with the tone's amplitude (Adler's equation).  Compare its phase noise with the MAX2871's.  The switch turns it off.

tiles.name: 1:1 transformer
tiles.result: 0.3 dB of loss at 10 MHz, 0.5 dB at 100 MHz, 1.8 dB at 500 MHz (the datasheet); OUT's shell is not ground
notes: Mini-Circuits TC1-1TG2+: two windings, so OUT's centre and shell are a balanced pair: a balun for a dipole (an SMA
to two-clip lead on OUT), or a break in a ground loop between the host and a mains-earthed instrument.  OUT's legs
are their own net with no copper of the board's ground within 5.6 mm on any layer.

tiles.name: 1:4 transformer
tiles.result: IN reads 50 ohm with switch 1 on (200 ohm across OUT) and 12.5 ohm with switch 2; OUT's voltage is twice IN's, 0.8 dB of loss at 10 MHz
notes: Mini-Circuits TC4-1W+: the secondary has twice the primary's turns, so it carries twice the voltage at half the
current and any load on OUT looks a quarter of itself at IN.  200 ohm on OUT (switch 1) is a match; 49.9 ohm (switch 2)
reads 12.5 ohm.  The centre tap is left open.

back_text: AMOD-P2: passive RF and analog blocks.  IN is each
tile's top-left jack, OUT its bottom-right.  No USB:
P22 and P23 run on the Pmod's 3.3 V when it is plugged
in; everything else needs nothing.  See the handbook.
